title: Adaptive Density & Visual Polish for Rollout Timeline and Cost Sparklines
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an adaptive density mode and final visual polish for the rollout timeline and associated cost sparklines so that users can scan health and cost signals at multiple densities (compact, default, expanded) without losing affordances for debugging. This ticket covers final design assets, redlines for dev, accessibility checks, and a short QA checklist for visual regressions.
design_goals: Support three density states (compact, default, expanded) for the rollout timeline and cost tiles
Preserve signal clarity at compact density: annotations for active canaries and failure markers must remain legible
Ensure sparklines convey both relative cost delta and outlier spikes with minimal ink
Provide clear hover/focus affordances for actionable items in compact mode
Meet color contrast and keyboard navigation accessibility requirements
decisions: Compact density will hide verbose labels and show iconography + tooltip on hover/focus
Sparklines will use two-tone encoding: primary line for baseline token cost, secondary overlay for rollout delta spikes
Failure markers use a consistent triangular glyph across the console to avoid ambiguity with alerts
Density toggles persist per-user in local storage with global override via team preferences
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates all three densities across at least three viewport widths
Redlines include spacing tokens, typography scales, and icon sizes for each density state
A11y report shows contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for critical labels and keyboard focus order verified
Dev handoff includes component states (default/hover/selected/disabled) and motion spec for density transitions
QA checklist catches visual regressions: sparkline baselines, marker placement, tooltip truncation
